Hello! Nice to meet you!

I would like to request an illustration of a fox girl character!

Please choose 1 fox girl to illustrate. 

Blue Ribbon Fox Girl
A cool and quiet girl, though she sometimes tries a little too hard to make those around her happy. The Blue Ribbon Fox Girl and the Red Ribbon Fox Girl are best friends. She is partnered with a fox spirit, who helps with household chores in exchange for meals. This fox girl’s name is “Iris,” the first of the fox fleet and my personal favorite OC. She has gone through several costume changes, but this fox girl is the one I use for most of my profile pictures. The blue ribbon fox is my “poster girl”.

Red Ribbon Fox Girl
She has a cold and distant personality and takes time to open her heart, but once she does, she loves forever. She is best friends with the Blue Ribbon Fox Girl and has a slightly tsundere personality. This fox girl’s name is Mariah, pronounced “Mirai-ah,” not “Maria.” Her design is based on the Blue Ribbon Fox Girl, Iris. As you can see from their contrasting differences, they are considered a duo. Both were designed by the same artist, and thus they share a special bond. The girl has two tails and signifies the second fox girl designed. Mariah’s hairstyle is also twin-tails.

Golden Ribbon Fox Girl
A heroine-type girl with cheat-level abilities who loves others unconditionally. For some reason, she enjoys staying close to the Red Ribbon Fox Girl, especially touching her tail (this may be due to the Golden Ribbon Fox’s design being partially based on the original Red Ribbon Fox design). In the original Red Ribbon Fox design, her tail ribbon had bells attached to her tail ribbons, and the Golden Ribbon Fox has one more tail than the Red Ribbon Fox to signify the third fox designed. The Red Ribbon Fox Girl, who is not used to such affection, is often overwhelmed and tries to push the Golden Ribbon Fox Girl away—but never succeeds. The Blue Ribbon Fox Girl is happy to see the Red Ribbon Fox Girl making a new friend. This fox girl’s name is Sana, named after her three large tails.  I had a plan to continually add tails for each new fox girl designed, But that idea was scrapped.

Green Ribbon Fox Girl
A noble lady who, due to her upbringing, has closed off her emotions and kept her distance from society. She lacks meaningful life experience and deeply longs for a best friend. The Green Ribbon Fox Girl is an amateur novelist, and the Blue Ribbon Fox Girl has read many of her works. While most of them are not very well written, the Blue Ribbon Fox Girl continues searching for hidden masterpieces. The Blue Ribbon Fox Girl does not know that the Green Ribbon Fox Girl is the author, but the Green Ribbon Fox Girl knows that the Blue Ribbon Fox Girl is one of her readers. She wishes to become the Blue Ribbon Fox Girl’s best friend—something that makes the Red Ribbon Fox Girl a little jealous. This fox girl’s name is “Eris,” a name similar to “Iris,” since her design is also based on the Blue Ribbon Fox Girl. Eris’s tail also has the same black tip as Iris’s. Her pen name is “Mido,” a shortened form of Midori, which was originally intended to be her real name.

Black Ribbon Fox Girl
The daughter of a military commander, she relies only on herself to survive. The Black Ribbon Fox Girl loves only under very specific conditions. She is acquainted with—or possibly friends with—the Green Ribbon Fox Girl, who is also her closest confidant. However, when she notices the Green Ribbon Fox Girl’s interest in the Blue Ribbon Fox Girl, she becomes protective. She starts copying the Blue Ribbon Fox Girl’s fashion and begins to see her as a rival—although the Blue Ribbon Fox Girl is completely unaware of this rivalry. The Black Ribbon Fox Girl is also a regular customer at the Brown Ribbon Fox Girl’s café. Because she is a noble with a poor sense of money, she overpays for coffee and ends up being the café’s biggest customer—and savior. Once she finds out she has been overpaying for coffee by the brown ribbon fox girl, the black ribbon fox girl’s pride keeps her from admitting she is out of touch with the world and keeps paying for the overpriced coffee, “coffee of this quality is worth it”. This fox girl’s name is Lunetta, named after her moon-shaped hair accessories. It is a Spanish word meaning “little moon.” Her design is also based on the Blue Ribbon Fox Girl.

White Ribbon Fox Girl
A stoic genius mage who values only her own happiness. Due to a harsh upbringing, she lacks empathy. She excels in star magic and loves observing shooting stars, but her magic often causes meteor showers, resulting in widespread environmental destruction. This fox girl’s name is “Astraea,” another word associated with stars. Astraea can transform into a black witch with a “black hole” motif. As Astraea becomes more obsessed with making shooting stars, her shooting stars collapse into black holes and her personality becomes the opposite of her usual stoic self—seductive, chaotic, and predatory, as if a witch has taken over and wants to swallow you whole. This black witch is a separate entity hidden inside Astraea’s halo.

Pink Ribbon Fox Girl
A chaotic shrine maiden who cares only about the happiness of others. A master of the Dance of Rainbows, she believes that summoning rainbows will make everyone happy. However, her dances tend to cause repeated torrential rains and environmental destruction. This fox girl’s name is “Niko.” Ni comes from the word Niji (rainbow), and Ko is added to make it a girl’s name. As Niko becomes more obsessed with creating rainbows,
Niko thoughts and eyes become foggy. Niko’s halo melts significantly and is a measure of her sanity. Niko transforms and takes on the “fogbow” motif. Instead of Rainbows for everyone to see, Niko now creates fogbows (color-less rainbows), rainbows which no-one can see.

Silver Ribbon Fox Girl
A diligent and overachieving cleric-type girl who is constantly plagued by misfortune. She holds the title of Auxiliary Bishop—a prestigious honor earned at a young age—but in reality, it is used as an excuse for the actual bishop to dump all daily work onto her. Her personality resembles that of an overworked office worker. Her motto is: “Smile. Nod. Endure.” This fox girl’s name is “Sylphy,” a feminine name reminiscent of the word silver and her color scheme.

Purple Ribbon Fox Girl
An elegant princess with the ability to read emotions. Because of this power, she is feared and avoided by others and lives a lonely life. She spends her days tending a garden of purple orchids. Her only friend is the Golden Ribbon Fox Girl, a descendant of a legendary hero’s bloodline who inherited the ability to block emotion reading. This fox girl is “Cattleya.” As her name suggests, she likes cattleya flowers. Her sister Rosalinde calls her Leya. Cattleya is the older sister.

Orange Ribbon Fox Girl
The younger sister of the Purple Ribbon Fox Girl and the second princess. To stand out in the political world, she plays the role of a villain, but internally she despises being seen as insane and feels deep shame over it. Her frequent misuse of emotion-reading abilities amplifies the nobles’ fear of both sisters. Her best friend is the Silver Ribbon Fox Girl, and both of them hide their true selves behind “masks.”This fox girl is Rosalinde, who likes roses. Rosalinde’s design is based on an orange rose. Her sister Leya calls her Rosa. She is the younger sister.

Navy Ribbon Fox Girl
A royal maid and retainer—though somewhat lacking in professionalism. She skillfully covers up laziness and mistakes with impressive excuses. She often serves tea claimed to be “good for your health” and infused with aromatherapy… but in reality, it’s just hot water served with a candle. She is Rosa’s second retainer. I commissioned this character as a counterpart to a maroon ribbon girl nicknamed “Assassin-chan”. She wears many navy-colored ribbons. I don’t have a finalized name for her, but “Lapis”would suit this blue-colored girl well.

Maroon Ribbon Fox Girl
A sensible and realistic girl. By day, she serves as a royal retainer; by night, she is a serious assassin. She is skeptical of everything the Navy Ribbon Fox Girl does, but her complaints are usually ignored. (“Wait… isn’t this just hot water?”) She is Rosa’s first retainer. This character was adopted from an auction I won and was originally named simply “Assassin-chan.” I don’t have a finalized name for her yet, but I think “Sena” fits—a beautiful yet embarrassing name for an assassin girl.

Brown Ribbon Fox Girl
A maid and café owner who specializes in producing exceptional coffee beans. Her family’s beans grant permanent stat-boosting effects, which lead to the Brown Ribbon Fox Girl gaining abnormal strength—she can crush coffee beans with one hand. She tolerates no criticism of her coffee, and when angered, transforms into a terrifyingly sweet-smiling girl. In the past, her family’s coffee was frequently criticized, and that old resentment became the driving force behind perfecting the ultimate cup. However, due to high production costs, her special coffee is extremely expensive. As a result, she also sells other sweets and drinks to keep her café running. She even works part-time jobs to make ends meet. This fox girl’s name is Moka, similar to the word mocha, which is coffee-related.

Anything is fine! 

Thank you for your time!
